human_tolerance.notes: In winter the species is familiar in and around towns and is in many places the most common bird at feeders; a rare vagrant to western Europe that usually winters in gardens.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Breeds in coniferous or mixed forest; normally two clutches of four eggs, eggs incubated by the female for 12 to 13 days and young leaving the nest 11 to 14 days after hatching.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: Winter birds forage in flocks that may contain several different subspecies; a flock of dark-eyed juncos has been known as a blizzard.

phases.name: absent
phases.note: Northern birds migrate further south, arriving in winter quarters between mid-September and November and leaving to breed from mid-March onwards, with almost all gone by the end of April; many populations are permanent residents or altitudinal migrants instead.

vocalizations.description: A trill similar to the chipping sparrow's, though the red-backed subspecies' song is more complex and similar to that of the yellow-eyed junco.
Tick sounds and very high-pitched tinkling chips, resembling the call of the black-throated blue warbler.

taxonomy.note: GBIF backbone gives family Passerellidae and authority (Linnaeus, 1758); ITIS scientific-name search returns TSN 179410 with the same authority.

external.note: GBIF usageKey 9362842 from species/match; ITIS TSN 179410 from the ITIS scientific-name search; NCBI taxon id 40217, eBird code daejun and IUCN category least concern (Q211005) from Wikidata P685, P3444 and P141.

range.note: Country list derived from the Description and Distribution sections: 'common across much of temperate North America and in summer it ranges far into the Arctic', with the gray-headed group breeding into Mexico and the Guadalupe junco (formerly a subspecies, now a separate species) endemic to Guadalupe Island off Mexico. Canada and Mexico added from the same range description; Greenland inferred from the Arctic summer range and omitted as uncertain, so not listed.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: 'These birds forage on the ground' by hopping, and by walking when undisturbed; white outer tail feathers flash 'while hopping on the ground'; plus powered flight.

traits.nest_type.note: 'Dark-eyed juncos usually nest in a cup-shaped depression on the ground, well-hidden by vegetation', 'although nests are sometimes found in the lower branches of a shrub or tree'. Ground chosen as the primary type.

traits.perching.note: Perches in shrubs and trees to roost and sing; nests occasionally in the lower branches of a shrub or tree.

traits.senses.note: Authored from the species' well-developed song and call repertoire ('excellent bird to study for learning bird language') and its ability to take seed visually at feeders; olfaction set to Low, no sourced claim found.

traits.size_class.note: From mass_kg (0.0195 kg falls in the Tiny band, under 0.05 kg).

traits.mass_kg.note: EltonTraits BirdFuncDat BodyMass-Value 19.5 g and AVONET Mass 19.5 g agree exactly (both sourced to Dunning 2008), and sit inside Wikipedia's 18-30 g range.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: 'Body mass can vary from 18 to 30 g'.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Judgement, and an honest gap: no openly licensed source consulted states a mean or typical longevity for this species. The USGS Patuxent Bird Banding Laboratory longevity table (public domain) holds the banded-bird maximum-age record, but it is rendered client-side and its value could not be read here, so it is not cited. 1.5 years is an authored order-of-magnitude figure for typical adult longevity of a small, largely migratory passerine, where first-year mortality dominates; treat it as a placeholder, not a measurement.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits Diet-Inv 30, Diet-Seed 70. Wikipedia's 'They mainly eat seeds and insects, with seeds comprising three quarters of their year-round diet' agrees with those shares; the same paragraph notes insects are nearly half the diet during the breeding season, which is why the invertebrate resource carries a breeding-season weighting in the notes rather than changing the annual fractions.

traits.social.note: 'In winter, they often forage in flocks that may contain several different subspecies'; breeding pairs are solitary, so Flock is the primary structure and the range 2-30 is an authored band informed by the winter-flocking description (a flock is called a blizzard).

traits.defense.note: Authored: the species flushes from the ground to a perch or into cover when approached, as described by its ground-foraging and roosting behaviour; no explicit 'defense' statement in the source.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: a bold, well-known feeder bird that is 'in many places the most common birds at feeders' and wintering in British gardens, so a low value.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits ForStrat-ground 60; ForStrat-understory 10 + ForStrat-midhigh 30 (40) mapped to arboreal.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Authored: roosts and sings from shrubs and low trees, so shrub_thicket; the source describes the roosting perch only indirectly.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet exactly. Nesting on the ground from the Breeding section. Perch and shrub_thicket shelter weights are authored judgement; no open source quantifies their relative use.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: 'In winter, dark-eyed juncos are familiar in and around towns, and in many places are the most common birds at feeders'; light_max is authored (judgement).

seasonal.strategy.note: 'Northern birds migrate further south, arriving in their winter quarters between mid-September and November and leaving to breed from mid-March onwards ... Many populations are permanent residents or altitudinal migrants'.

seasonal.winter_fraction.note: Judgement: the source states that many populations are permanent residents or altitudinal migrants while northern birds migrate, without giving a proportion, so 0.4 is an authored figure for the share of the species' population that overwinters on its breeding grounds.

seasonal.phases.note: Breeding window from 'normally two clutches of four eggs are laid during the breeding season', incubation of 12-13 days and fledging at 11-14 days, applied to the April-August breeding season in the southern part of the range; winter flocking window from the same distribution paragraph; the regional absent phase from the mid-September to end-April migration window. Exact window edges are judgements informed by those dates.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Juvenile duration from 'juveniles ... acquire adult plumage at two to three months' (75 days used, the midpoint) and fledging 11-14 days after hatching; scale is authored judgement and the egg stage carries no duration because none is sourced.

vocalizations.alarm.note: 'Calls include tick sounds and very high-pitched tinkling chips' from the Description section.

vocalizations.note: Descriptions and contexts from the Description section; months, time windows and cooldowns are authored judgement, since no open source quantifies them. No open source gives frequency bands, so freq_hz is omitted.

look.note: Colours from the Description section ('gray heads, necks, and breasts, gray or brown backs and wings, and a white belly', bill 'usually pale pinkish', 'white outer tail feathers'); the tail is coloured from the belly slot to render the white outer tail. Proportions are authored judgement for a stocky, short-tailed sparrow.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program. food_tag set to seed (the dominant annual diet share) rather than the program's invertebrate default; nest_m1/nest_m2 widened to April-August to cover two clutches on or near the ground.
